7.text: later in life than do those of the Maritime Chukchee, and give as a reason

20.text: When refused by a woman, they are inclined to violence and rape. Many

21.text: of their pet names and nicknames are very obscene.

22.text: Their endurance in undergoing cold, hunger, and various hardships, is very

23.text: great. Small children are left all day in the open air in winter. I have seen

24.text: infants lying on the snow attempt to get out of their fur combination-suits.

25.text: The upper part of their bodies remained naked for a long time, yet they did

26.text: not show any signs of discomfort, though the cold was severe and the wind

27.text: blew sharply. The women work with the needle in the open air even in

28.text: March, at a temperature of 30° below zero, Centigrade. Their fingers remain

29.text: unprotected for several hours at a stretch. The exertion even makes them

30.text: feel warm and perspire so, that they throw aside their ample fur bodices and

31.text: remain half naked, or else even thrust large cakes of snow into their bosoms.

32.text: The reindeer-hunters frequently start out with very little food, depending

33.text: upon future quarry for their sustenance. When unsuccessful, they get along

34.text: on very little food for several days, and all the while display the utmost agility

35.text: in walking about and searching for game. Reindeer herdsmen, men or women,

36.text: often go without sleep for two or three days. A young girl will work for a

37.text: whole day on skins, then watch the herd all night long, and in the morning

38.text: return home and busy herself till evening, without any visible strain upon her
